questions.prompt: What are Request Units per second (RU/s) in Cosmos DB?

options.text: The number of regions your data is replicated to
The currency measuring the throughput/cost of operations
The maximum size of a single item
The number of consistency levels available

questions.explanation: RU/s is the currency for throughput and cost — a single unit bundles the CPU, memory, and I/O an operation uses. You provision RU/s or use serverless pay-per-request.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Cosmos DB are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: A good partition key has high cardinality and spreads load evenly
A poor partition key can create a hot partition that gets throttled
Session is the default consistency level
The partition key is trivial to change after the fact

questions.explanation: Good keys are high-cardinality and even; poor keys cause hot partitions; Session is the default. The partition key is a foundational choice that's hard to change later.

questions.prompt: The default Cosmos DB consistency level, which guarantees you read your own writes within a client session, is ____.
questions.explanation: Session is the default — consistent within a client session (read your own writes) — offering much better latency and availability than Strong.

questions.prompt: Order the five consistency levels from STRONGEST to WEAKEST.
questions.explanation: The spectrum runs Strong, Bounded staleness, Session, Consistent prefix, Eventual — trading consistency for lower latency and higher availability.

questions.prompt: Match each Cosmos DB concept to its meaning.

pairs.right: The native document API for new apps
Property that distributes data across partitions
Overloaded partition from a poor key choice

questions.explanation: NoSQL is the native API; the partition key distributes data; a hot partition is overloaded; RU/s measures throughput/cost.
